subject: Retention defaults and residency for prompts vs outputs — BrightBank Q&A

Subject: Quick Q: what do you retain by default (prompts vs outputs)?

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightBank security team asked for a short clarification so they can complete our vendor questionnaire. Two quick things: 1) what does Redwood retain by default from an API request (the raw prompt/user input vs the model output/answer), and 2) are any of those items routed or stored outside of EU regions by default?

They specifically flagged streamed tokens (we stream partial responses to users) and KV/cache artifacts from conversational sessions — are those treated as persistent logs or ephemeral?

If you can point me to a short summary (or attach something we can drop into the questionnaire) that would be great.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Lead Information Security, BrightBank

Hi Alex — thanks for the question and for raising the security team's concern. I attached a short one-page summary that should map cleanly into your questionnaire (redwood-retention-summary.pdf). Top-level answers up front:

- By default we persist final request and final model response (the API payloads) for 30 days to support debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
- Prefixes/streamed partial tokens are considered ephemeral; we do not persist streamed intermediate tokens beyond the session unless a customer explicitly enables session transcripts.
- KV cache artifacts (runtime-only caches used to accelerate repeats within a session) are ephemeral and do not persist to long-term storage by default.
- For EU-region customers we store all persisted artifacts within the customer-chosen EU region by default (no cross-border routing unless explicitly configured).

I'll loop in Connor for a quick technical confirmation on the streaming/KV details (I want to make sure the wording is precise for audit purposes) and Kim for legal/policy nuance on the retention window and erasure options.

If the attached doesn't hit everything, happy to hop on a 20-minute call with your security team.

Connor / Kim — forwarding BrightBank's ask below. My short answers are in the attached summary but can you confirm the following bullets before I send a final, slightly more formal response to Alex and their security team?

Questions to confirm:
1) Default persisted window: 30 days for final request/response payloads (used for billing, debugging, evals). Is that still accurate for Hosted customers?
2) Streaming tokens: we do not persist intermediate partial tokens across sessions by default — only final assembled responses are persisted unless session-transcript is enabled. Confirm behavior for streaming-enabled routes (server-side): are there logs that capture individual delta tokens in any long-term store?
3) KV cache: runtime caches are ephemeral and tied to the serving instance’s lifecycle; they are not written to persistent object storage by default. Confirm there are no background drains to durable storage.
4) EU residency: for customers who select an EU region we keep persisted artifacts in-region; are there any telemetry or aggregated metrics that leave EU by default?

Thanks — if easier, a quick reply inline is fine. I want to get this back to them today.

Marissa / Kim — brief technical confirmations below, feel free to copy/paste into a customer-facing note.

1) Default persisted window: Hosted API persists final request and final response payloads for 30 days by default. This is configurable for enterprise/Dedicated customers via account settings and can be shortened by request; Private customers manage retention locally.

2) Streaming tokens: our streaming pathway assembles deltas on the serving node and transmits them to the client in near-real time. We do not persist each delta token to long-term storage by default. There are short-lived in-memory buffers and transient logs for debugging (rotated quickly and not moved to durable store). If a customer turns on \"session transcripts\" or explicitly requests a transcript export, the final assembled transcript is persisted according to the account retention policy.

3) KV cache: KV caches reside in-process or on local instance NVMe and are considered ephemeral. They are not periodically flushed to durable object storage by default. For Dedicated/Private installs customers can opt to hook KV snapshots to their own object storage, but that's an opt-in enterprise configuration. No background drain to durable storage for Hosted customers without an explicit config.

4) EU residency & telemetry: For customers who select EU region we store persisted artifacts (requests/responses, exports) in-region. We do send aggregated telemetry/usage metrics (token counts, latencies) to our global control plane for operational monitoring, but those metrics are aggregated, non-identifiable, and do not include raw prompts or model outputs. If a customer requires that telemetry remain in-region, we can offer Private deployments or Enterprise data residency options where telemetry is scoped to the customer's region.

Also note: attachments referenced in our shared summary (redwood-retention-summary.pdf) include the exact policy language and where to find the erase/runbook procedure.

Alex — thanks for the patience. Connor and Kim confirmed the technical and policy points; summary below and attached copy of the one-pager + the questionnaire we filled out (brightbank-questionnaire.xlsx).

Short summary for questionnaire:
- Default retention: final request (prompt) and final response (model output) are persisted for 30 days by default for Hosted API customers.
- Streaming tokens: intermediate/partial streamed tokens are ephemeral and are not written to long-term storage by default (unless session transcripts are enabled).
- KV cache: runtime-only, ephemeral; not persisted to durable storage without opt-in.
- EU residency: persisted artifacts for customers who choose EU region remain in-region by default. Aggregated operational telemetry (non-identifiable token counts/latency) may be processed by our global control plane; raw prompts/responses are not sent out of-region.
